Name: an
name: An
domain_and_role: the foreigners' sky worship; his two sons came to rule the City of the Abyss and the City of Kings

Name: enlil
name: Enlil
domain_and_role: kingship; the legacy of kings is mummified and guarded at his city

Name: enki
name: Enki
domain_and_role: saw that men became unworthy and ended the golden age; sent the flood; the god of magic (designer ruling D-016) — the sea gems are his gifts and extensions of his power

Name: utu
name: Utu
domain_and_role: the sun; the Retributors of Utu are his paladin guild

Name: nanna
name: Nanna
domain_and_role: the moon

Name: inanna
name: Inanna
also_known_as: Ishtar; the lady of the skies
domain_and_role: the Empire's patron: tribute and conquest in her honor; described as a demonic entity by the Brotherhood; the Sumerian ending names her cult
cult_sites: city_of_the_sky (cult center of the Sky Father and the Lady of the Skies)

Name: abzu
name: Abzu
domain_and_role: primordial water (cf. the City of the Abyss's worship)

Name: the_two_waters
name: the deities of salt and fresh water
domain_and_role: the southern armada's gods; first great temple; sacrifices of fish and sea gems

Name: water_lord
name: Water Lord
domain_and_role: the two-waters worship of the City of the Abyss shifted to him under northern rule

Name: underworld_queen
name: the queen of the underworld
also_known_as: earth mother of the underworld (at Gravestone)
domain_and_role: the dead cult; great statue in the temple built within the earth. Ruling (D-018): City of the Dead and Gravestone are ONE city — Gravestone (e-ab-kur-irkalla-ki) is its native cultic name
cult_sites: city_of_the_dead = gravestone (one city; D-018 resolves game-design §11.7's ambiguity)
source_ref: wb §5; notes L44;L103; D-018 (the notes give one dead-cult city under two names: a capital and its temple-name; the same pattern as City of Jewels/the Law Giver's capital)

Name: taurissian_former_sun_god
name: the former sun god of the Taurissian people
domain_and_role: the City of the Warrior Spirit was once his city

Name: gugalanna
name: Gugalanna
also_known_as: the Bull of Heaven; the empire of the bull
domain_and_role: the hidden evil of the Sumerian ending (endings §3.2): an ancient contemporary of Ishtar; consort of the underworld queen; biding in the dead cult's own shadow until Ishtar's cult is torn down and the throne-room empties for him
cult_sites: city_of_the_dead = gravestone (his cult grows there first)
source_ref: Epic of Gilgamesh (Gugalanna; the Bull of Heaven; husband of Ereshkigal; slain by Gilgamesh and Enkidu) grounding endings §3.2's unnamed 'empire of the bull'; D-018

Name: the_eight_of_medicine
name: the 8 deities of medicine
also_known_as: resolved by the eight rows below: Gula; Ninisina; Ninkarrak; Nintinugga; Damu; Ninazu; Baba; Meme
source_ref: notes L97 (list unwritten); D-018 — grounded in the real Mesopotamian medicine-deity circle rather than invented from nothing

Name: gula
name: Gula
domain_and_role: chief goddess of healing; her dog is her emblem and sits at sickbeds; oversees exorcist-physicians in the temple of sun and moon's scribal-school slot
cult_sites: city_of_the_moon (the temple of sun and moon's physicians answer to her)
source_ref: attested Mesopotamian healing-goddess tradition (Gula/Bau syncretism; dog iconography; Old Babylonian and later healing incantations); D-018

Name: ninisina
name: Ninisina
domain_and_role: healing goddess later merged with Gula; patroness of physicians and midwives
source_ref: attested Mesopotamian medicine-goddess tradition (Ninisina/Gula syncretism); D-018

Name: ninkarrak
name: Ninkarrak
domain_and_role: healing goddess invoked in medical incantations and on amulets against disease
source_ref: attested Mesopotamian medicine-goddess tradition (Ninkarrak invoked in incantation and amulet texts); D-018

Name: nintinugga
name: Nintinugga
also_known_as: she who restores the dead to life
domain_and_role: healing goddess of Nippur; invoked at the sickbed
cult_sites: city_of_kings (Nippur's own healing goddess; fitting Enlil's city)
source_ref: attested Mesopotamian medicine-goddess tradition (Nintinugga of Nippur); D-018

Name: damu
name: Damu
domain_and_role: god of healing and vegetation; the weeping god who dies and returns; invoked over the sick
source_ref: attested Mesopotamian healing-god tradition (Damu; dying-and-returning healing god); D-018

Name: ninazu
name: Ninazu
domain_and_role: healing god with underworld ties — physician of the netherworld as well as the living
cult_sites: city_of_the_dead = gravestone (his underworld face fits the dead cult's city)
source_ref: attested Mesopotamian healing-god tradition (Ninazu; herbal medicine and underworld associations); D-018

Name: baba
name: Baba
domain_and_role: healing goddess of Lagash; tends the sick alongside Gula in the later syncretism
source_ref: attested Mesopotamian healing-goddess tradition (Baba/Bau of Lagash); D-018

Name: meme
name: Meme
domain_and_role: daughter or handmaid of Gula in her healing circle; a minor healing presence at the sickbed
source_ref: attested Mesopotamian healing-goddess tradition (Meme; Gula's circle); D-018
